title: B1 · Intermediate
description: Express opinions, talk about experiences and plans, and understand connected speech and real-world listening.

objectives.can_do: I can talk about experiences using the present perfect and the past simple.
objectives.title: Experiences: present perfect vs past simple

activities.instruction: Talk about three experiences you have had and say when they happened.
activities.target: I have been to ... / I went there in ... / I have never ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say the difference between the present perfect and the past simple.
activities.target: present perfect = experience / past simple = finished time

activities.instruction: Talk about an experience of a friend using the present perfect and the past simple.
activities.target: He/She has ... / He/She went there in ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can talk about experiences using the present perfect and the past simple.

activities.instruction: On your own, tell the tutor about three experiences you have had and say when they happened.
activities.target: I have been to ... / I went there in ...

checks.prompt: Choose the correct sentence:
options: I have seen that film last week.
I saw that film last week.
I have saw that film last week.

checks.prompt: Choose the correct sentence:
options: She has never been to London.
She have never been to London.
She never has been to London.

checks.prompt: Which word means 'hasta ahora' in 'I have not finished it ___'?

objectives.can_do: I can talk about unfinished time using 'yet' and 'already'.
objectives.title: Yet and already

activities.instruction: Say two things you have already done today and one thing you have not done yet.
activities.target: I have already ... / I have not ... yet.

activities.instruction: Without looking, say where 'yet' and 'already' go in a sentence.
activities.target: already = affirmative / yet = negative and questions

activities.instruction: Talk about what a friend has already done or has not done yet today.
activities.target: He/She has already ... / He/She has not ... yet.

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can talk about unfinished time using 'yet' and 'already'.

activities.instruction: On your own, say two things you have already done and one thing you have not done yet.
activities.target: I have already ... / I have not ... yet.

checks.prompt: Choose the correct sentence:
options: I have not finished my homework yet.
I have not finished my homework already.
I not have finished my homework yet.

checks.prompt: Choose the correct sentence:
Which word is used in negative sentences and questions to mean 'todavía'?

objectives.can_do: I can give and justify my opinions on everyday topics.
objectives.title: Giving opinions

activities.instruction: Give and justify your opinion about working from home.
activities.target: In my opinion ... because ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say three phrases that introduce a personal opinion.
activities.target: In my opinion / I think / From my point of view

activities.instruction: Give and justify your opinion about a topic you have not discussed in this lesson.
activities.target: In my opinion ... because ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can give and justify my opinions on everyday topics.

activities.instruction: On your own, give and justify your opinion about working from home.
activities.target: In my opinion ... because ...

checks.prompt: Which phrase introduces a personal opinion?
Which word means 'tener la misma opinión'?

objectives.can_do: I can agree and disagree politely in a conversation.
objectives.title: Agreeing and disagreeing

activities.instruction: Disagree politely with the tutor's opinion about social media.
activities.target: I see your point, but ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say two ways to disagree politely.
activities.target: I see your point, but ... / That is a good point, however ...

activities.instruction: Disagree politely with an opinion you have not discussed in this lesson.
activities.target: I see your point, but ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can agree and disagree politely in a conversation.

activities.instruction: On your own, disagree politely with the tutor's opinion about social media.
activities.target: I see your point, but ...

checks.prompt: Which phrase politely introduces a disagreement?
Which word means 'no estar de acuerdo'?

objectives.can_do: I can understand two people exchanging opinions and identify agreement and disagreement.
objectives.title: Listening to opinions

activities.instruction: Listen to a short conversation and say who agrees and who disagrees.
activities.target: A agrees / B disagrees because ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say two phrases that show agreement and two that show disagreement.
activities.target: I agree / that is a good point / I see your point, but / I am not sure

activities.instruction: Describe a conversation where you agreed or disagreed with someone, outside this lesson.
activities.target: I agreed because ... / I disagreed because ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can understand two people exchanging opinions.

activities.instruction: On your own, listen and identify the speakers' opinions.
activities.target: The first speaker thinks ... / the second disagrees because ...

checks.prompt: You hear: 'I think working from home is great, but I see what you mean about missing colleagues.' How does the speaker feel?
You hear: 'That's a good point, actually.' What is the speaker doing?
Which phrase shows polite disagreement?

objectives.can_do: I can link my opinions using discourse markers like 'firstly', 'however' and 'for example'.
objectives.title: Linking opinions with discourse markers

activities.instruction: Write two opinions linked with 'firstly' and 'however'.
activities.target: Firstly, I think ... / However, on the other hand ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say three discourse markers that link ideas.
activities.target: firstly / however / for example

activities.instruction: Give an opinion about a new topic using two discourse markers you have not practised.
activities.target: On the other hand ... / for example ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can link my opinions using discourse markers.

activities.instruction: On your own, write two opinions linked with discourse markers.
activities.target: Firstly ... / However ... / for example ...

checks.prompt: Which phrase introduces a contrast?
Which phrase gives an example?
Which phrase adds a second point?

objectives.can_do: I can talk about future plans and predictions.
objectives.title: Future: will, going to, present continuous

activities.instruction: Talk about your plans for next weekend and a prediction about the future.
activities.target: I am going to ... / I will probably ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say the three ways to talk about the future.
activities.target: will / going to / present continuous

activities.instruction: Predict what a friend will do next weekend, not what you will do.
activities.target: He/She will probably ... / is going to ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can talk about future plans and predictions.

activities.instruction: On your own, talk about your plans for next weekend and a prediction about the future.
activities.target: I am going to ... / I will probably ...

checks.prompt: Choose the correct sentence for a plan:
options: I am going to visit my aunt.
I will to visit my aunt.

checks.prompt: Choose the correct sentence for a prediction:
options: I think it will rain tomorrow.
I think it is going rain tomorrow.

checks.prompt: Which word means 'un plan para el futuro'?

objectives.can_do: I can use the first conditional to talk about possibilities.
objectives.title: First conditional

activities.instruction: Say what you will do if it rains this weekend.
activities.target: If it rains, I will ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say the two parts of a first conditional sentence.
activities.target: if + present simple / will + infinitive

activities.instruction: Say what a friend will do in a situation you have not discussed.
activities.target: If ..., he/she will ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can use the first conditional to talk about possibilities.

activities.instruction: On your own, say what you will do if it rains this weekend.
activities.target: If it rains, I will ...

checks.prompt: Choose the correct sentence:
options: If it rains, I will stay at home.
If it will rain, I stay at home.
If it rained, I will stay at home.

checks.prompt: Choose the correct sentence:
options: Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.
Unless you will hurry, you miss the bus.
Unless you hurry, you miss the bus.

checks.prompt: Which word means 'si no'?

objectives.can_do: I can understand people discussing future plans and arrangements.
objectives.title: Listening to plans

activities.instruction: Listen to a conversation about plans and say what each person is going to do.
activities.target: A is going to ... / B will probably ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say two ways people talk about future plans.
activities.target: going to for plans / will for predictions

activities.instruction: Describe plans you heard about outside this lesson.
activities.target: They are going to ... / They will probably ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can understand people discussing future plans.

activities.instruction: On your own, listen and say what each person is going to do.
activities.target: A is going to ... / B will probably ...

checks.prompt: You hear: 'I'm going to visit my aunt this weekend, and I'll probably stay until Sunday.' What is the speaker going to do?
You hear: 'We'll probably cancel the picnic if it rains.' What will they most likely do?
Which word means 'un plan para el futuro'?

objectives.can_do: I can talk about rules and obligations using 'have to' and 'must'.
objectives.title: Obligation: have to / must

activities.instruction: Describe two rules at your job or school.
activities.target: At work I have to ... / I must ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say the difference between 'have to' and 'must'.
activities.target: have to = external rule / must = personal obligation

activities.instruction: Describe a rule in a place you have not talked about in this lesson.
activities.target: You have to ... / You must ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can talk about rules and obligations using 'have to' and 'must'.

activities.instruction: On your own, describe two rules at your job or school.
activities.target: At work I have to ... / I must ...

checks.prompt: Choose the correct sentence (external rule):
options: You have to wear a uniform.
You must to wear a uniform.

checks.prompt: Choose the sentence that means there is NO obligation:
options: You don't have to come early.

checks.prompt: Which word means 'una norma'?

objectives.can_do: I can make suggestions and respond to plans in a conversation.
objectives.title: Making suggestions and responding

activities.instruction: Suggest a plan for the weekend and respond to the tutor's idea.
activities.target: Why don't we ... / That sounds good, but ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say two ways to make a suggestion and one polite way to refuse.
activities.target: Why don't we ... / How about ... / I'd rather not ...

activities.instruction: Make a suggestion about a plan you have not discussed in this lesson.
activities.target: How about ... / Perhaps we could ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can make suggestions and respond to plans.

activities.instruction: On your own, suggest a plan and respond to the tutor's idea.
activities.target: Why don't we ... / That sounds good, but ...

checks.prompt: Which phrase makes a suggestion?
Which phrase politely refuses a suggestion?
Which phrase accepts a suggestion?

objectives.can_do: I can understand common connected speech forms like 'gonna' and 'wanna'.
objectives.title: Connected speech: gonna / wanna / didja

activities.instruction: Listen to connected speech and write the full form of each phrase.
activities.target: gonna → going to

activities.instruction: Without looking, say what 'gonna' and 'wanna' mean.
activities.target: gonna = going to / wanna = want to

activities.instruction: Explain a connected-speech phrase you heard outside this lesson.
activities.target: gotta / didja / couldja

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can understand common connected speech forms.

activities.instruction: On your own, give the full form of two connected-speech phrases you hear.
activities.target: gonna → going to / didja → did you

checks.prompt: You hear: 'I'm gonna call you later.' What does 'gonna' mean?
You hear: 'Didja see the match?' What does 'didja' mean?
Which word is the informal contraction of 'want to'?

objectives.can_do: I can understand the main idea and key details of a short narrative.
objectives.title: Narrative listening: gist and detail

activities.instruction: Listen to a short story and identify the main idea and two key details.
activities.target: The story is about ... / The key details are ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say the difference between the main idea and a detail.
activities.target: main idea = what the story is about / detail = specific fact

activities.instruction: Tell the main idea and two details of a story you heard outside this lesson.
activities.target: The story is about ... / The details are ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can understand the main idea and key details of a short narrative.

activities.instruction: On your own, listen to a short story and identify the main idea and two key details.
activities.target: The story is about ... / The key details are ...

checks.prompt: You hear: 'Last weekend we drove to the coast and, although it rained, we still had a great time.' What is the main idea?
options: They enjoyed a trip to the coast.

checks.prompt: Read: 'Maria missed her train, but she caught the next one and arrived on time.' What happened?
options: She arrived on time despite missing the first train.

checks.prompt: Which phrase means 'la idea principal'?

objectives.can_do: I can report what someone said using reported speech.
objectives.title: Reported speech

activities.instruction: Report what the tutor said in the previous exercise.
activities.target: He/She said that ... / He/She told me that ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say how 'will' changes in reported speech.
activities.target: will → would / said that / told me

activities.instruction: Report something a friend said, outside this lesson.
activities.target: He/She said that ... / He/She told me that ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can report what someone said using reported speech.

activities.instruction: On your own, report what the tutor said in the previous exercise.
activities.target: He/She said that ... / He/She told me that ...

checks.prompt: Choose the correct reported speech:
options: She said that she was tired.
She said that she is tired.

checks.prompt: Choose the correct reported speech:
options: He told me that he would call later.
He told me that he will call later.
He told that he would call later.

checks.prompt: Which word means 'decir a alguien'?

objectives.can_do: I can retell what I heard in my own words.
objectives.title: Retelling a narrative

activities.instruction: Listen to a short story and retell it in your own words.
activities.target: First ... / Then ... / Finally ...

activities.instruction: Without looking, say three words that show the order of events.
activities.target: first / then / finally

activities.instruction: Retell a story you heard outside this lesson, using sequence words.
activities.target: First ... / After that ... / Finally ...

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can retell what I heard in my own words.

activities.instruction: On your own, retell a short story in your own words.
activities.target: First ... / Then ... / Finally ...

checks.prompt: You hear: 'First we boarded the train, then we found our seats, and finally we ordered lunch.' What happened right after boarding the train?
Which word signals the last event in a sequence?

objectives.can_do: I can react naturally to what someone says in a conversation.
objectives.title: Reacting in conversation

activities.instruction: Listen to the tutor's news and react naturally, then ask a follow-up question.
activities.target: Really? / That's interesting. / What happened next?

activities.instruction: Without looking, say three natural reactions to someone's news.
activities.target: Really? / That's interesting / I see

activities.instruction: React to a piece of news you have not discussed in this lesson.
activities.target: That's interesting. / What happened next?

activities.instruction: In one sentence, say what you learned to do in this unit.
activities.target: I can react naturally to what someone says in a conversation.

activities.instruction: On your own, react naturally to the tutor's news and ask a follow-up question.
activities.target: Really? / That's interesting. / What happened next?

checks.prompt: Which word shows surprise at someone's news?
Which phrase asks someone to continue their story?

objectives.can_do: I can express opinions, talk about the future and understand connected speech.
objectives.title: Conversación final B1
concepts: review: opinions, future, obligations, connected speech

activities.instruction: Discuss your plans and opinions with the tutor, using connected speech naturally.
activities.target: B1 level conversation

checks.prompt: Choose the correct sentence:
options: If I have time, I will call you.
If I will have time, I call you.
If I have time, I call you.

checks.prompt: Choose the correct sentence:
options: You don't have to stay if you're busy.
You don't have stay if you're busy.
You don't has to stay if you're busy.

checks.prompt: Which phrase means 'en mi opinión'?
Which word is the informal contraction of 'going to'?
Listen: 'I'm gonna be a bit late, sorry.' What does the speaker mean?
Listen: 'Unless we hurry, we'll miss the start of the film.' What do they need to do?

objectives.can_do: I can hold a natural B1 conversation using everything I have learned.
objectives.title: Conversación integrada B1
concepts: review: opinions, future, obligations, connected speech, interaction

activities.instruction: Tell a short story and react to the tutor's questions and comments.
activities.target: B1 level conversation with opinions, plans and reactions

activities.instruction: Without looking, list three things you can now do in English at B1 level.
activities.target: express opinions / talk about plans / understand connected speech

activities.instruction: Use everything you have learned to talk about a completely new situation.
activities.target: B1 level conversation in a new context

checks.prompt: Choose the correct sentence:
options: She told me that she would arrive soon.
She told me that she will arrive soon.
She told that she would arrive soon.

checks.prompt: You hear: 'That's a good point, but I see it differently.' What is the speaker doing?
Which phrase makes a suggestion?
